debug.exported:
**Debug file created**

1. Download it: {download} (the link works for {hours} hours, the file is also saved as `{file}` in the config folder).
2. [Open a GitHub issue]({issue}) - the version and the time are filled in.
3. Describe what happened, when it happened and what you expected, and drag the file into the field *Debug file*.

Create the file as soon as possible after the problem: it holds the latest calculations and log messages.

The file contains your settings, prices, energy history and plans, the blueprint automations and the integrations and device models you use. Names, entity names, serial numbers, coordinates, notify services, addresses and keys are removed or replaced. Nothing is sent anywhere - you decide what you upload.

entity_description.what_if_day_tuesday: Smart is used in What-if on connections that end on Tuesday when the days are set to Selected days.

entity_description.run_what_if: Calculates what CJP charged against Smart and charging at once from the recorded history, with the same driving, prices and charging loss. It never changes the plan, the settings, the car or the charger.
entity_description.what_if: The adjusted cost difference of the latest What-if (CJP minus charging at once); negative means CJP was cheaper. The result is in the attributes.
entity_description.what_if_min_daily_battery_level: An alternative daily reserve (the battery level the car should still have when it comes home) for the What-if settings calculation only; 0 uses the current setting. It never changes the live setting.
entity_description.what_if_max_recommended_battery_level: A maximum recommended battery level for the What-if calculations only: the level Smart and charging at once charge to in the comparison with CJP, and the alternative level in the comparison of settings; 0 uses the current setting. It never changes the live setting.
entity_description.run_what_if_settings: Calculates the What-if for the daily reserve and the maximum recommended level from the recorded history, against the current settings. It never changes the plan, the settings, the car or the charger.
entity_description.what_if_settings: The adjusted cost difference of the latest What-if settings calculation (alternative settings minus current settings); negative means cheaper. The result is in the attributes.
entity_description.what_if_solar: The solar advantage of the completed months in the What-if EV solar comparison (the grid cost of the EV solar energy minus the sale it replaced); positive means solar was cheaper. Charging hours estimated from hourly averages (where no recorded session covers the time) are an upper bound; the result says when they are included and how much they hold. The result is in the attributes.
entity_description.run_what_if_no_solar: Calculates the charging planned from the grid only (no solar) over the selected period, with the current reserve and maximum level and the recorded driving, and compares it with what CJP recorded. It never changes the plan, the settings, the car or the charger.
entity_description.what_if_no_solar: The difference vs plan of the latest What-if without solar: the recorded cost minus the recorded energy at the planned grid price per kWh; positive means the recorded charging cost more. It is not the value of the solar energy (it also holds charging times and price choices). The result is in the attributes.

entity_help.soc_charge_power: The model learns from stable measurements how much power the car takes at different battery levels. A limit only enters the plan when the power is clearly lower than at lower levels over several charges. Until a level has its own measurements, stable hourly figures from Home Assistant's statistics are used as a starting value (marked 📊). The limit only affects the power the plan calculates with, not the control of the charger.
entity_help.learn_distance: The odometer is read every evening, and CJP suggests a driving distance per weekday from the last 8 weeks, even when the switch is off. When it is on, the work plan uses the higher of the entered and learned distance (at least 3 measured days for the day), and Optimal weekly charging likewise uses the higher one for the typical daily distance (at least 14 measured days). Entered numbers are not changed; the suggestions are shown under Analysis.
entity_help.public_charging:
When a public charging session ends (charge port/cable used away from home), Public charging session done turns on and you get a notification.
• Enter the total amount in Public charging session cost.
• The session is added to the charging history about 1 min after entering it.
• Enter -1 to ignore the session.
entity_help.forced_charging:
Forced charging can be enabled manually when the battery level is under the daily minimum.
• Charging: charges up to the daily minimum ({min_daily_battery_level} %).
• Cost control: no charging in the most expensive hours (see the attribute expensive_hours).
entity_help.manual_charging:
Manual charging starts charging at once without waiting for the plan.
• Allow manual charging now: charges with max current from the grid and solar.
• Solar only: charges only with the solar surplus.
Both are turned off automatically when the car is plugged in again.
entity_help.cheap_targets:
Charge targets at cheap prices:
• Very cheap target ({charge_very_cheap_battery_level} %): when the price is at most the average of the cheapest known prices of the coming week.
• Ultra cheap target ({charge_ultra_cheap_battery_level} %): when the price is another 25 % lower.
The targets follow the expected solar surplus of the coming week.
entity_help.trip:
Trip charging is planned automatically when:
• Trip charge percent is above 0 %, or Trip range needed is above 0 {distance}.
• Trip departure and Trip homecoming are set in the future.
It charges what the trip needs (from the percent or the distance). Charging between {max_recommended_charge_limit_battery_level}-100 % happens in the last hours before departure, finishing a little before it, to protect the battery. If the target cannot be reached, it charges what it can before departure.
Trip reset clears the trip; it is also reset automatically 2 hours after departure.
entity_help.solar_charging:
Enabled when there is solar surplus.
• Charging: uses the surplus; switches between 1 and 3 phases depending on it.
• Need: follows the surplus compared to the house consumption. Max charge {max_recommended_charge_limit_battery_level} %.
• Available solar power: shows the power available in watts during the current hour.
• Plan: the expected surplus of the week is used by Optimal weekly charging and Work plan charging, so the car charges as much solar as possible.

{charging_amps_table}
entity_help.fill_up:
Optimal weekly charging can be used on holiday (ignores the work plan).
Every day: always enough for the typical daily distance ({typical_daily_distance} {distance}) plus the daily minimum ({min_daily_battery_level} %), in the cheapest hours of the day.
The rest up to the max recommended ({max_recommended_charge_limit_battery_level} %) only in the cheapest hours of the week (the cheapest 30 %), and only when the next 24 hours are not clearly cheaper.
entity_help.workplan:
Work plan charging: enable when you work within the next week.
• Charging: plans daily charging over a week from workdays and days off.
• Need: uses departure and homecoming time and the distance of every workday. Minimum battery level at homecoming {min_daily_battery_level} %, max charge {max_recommended_charge_limit_battery_level} %.
• Plan: picks the cheapest available times before the workday departure; whether the target is reached depends on the charging windows and the amount of charging needed.
entity_help.full_charge: Recommended full charge: with an LFP battery a full charge is recommended at least every 14 days or as the car maker says. Set the number of days here; the last full charge is registered automatically.
entity_help.charging_loss:
Charging loss calculation – best result when charging from a low level (e.g. 10 %) to 100 %:
1. Discharge the car as much as possible (max 20 %).
2. Set the wanted charge limit in the car and Max recommended charge limit (now {max_recommended_charge_limit_battery_level} %, at least 90 %).
3. Turn on Calculate charging loss and let the car report when it is full.
4. The result is saved in the options automatically and you get a notification.
entity_help.cheap_limits:
Charge level at cheap prices:
• Very cheap: when the price is at most the average of the cheapest known prices of the coming week, charge to {very_cheap_grid_charging_max_battery_level} %.
• Ultra cheap: when the price is another 25 % lower, charge to {ultra_cheap_grid_charging_max_battery_level} %.
Used by planned charging hours at these prices, and always when "Charge on cheap power" is enabled.
entity_help.battery_preheat:
Battery level and preheating settings:
• Minimum daily battery level ({min_daily_battery_level} %): on returning from work or daily driving.
• Minimum trip battery level ({min_trip_battery_level} %): at homecoming from a trip.
• Minimum charge limit ({min_charge_limit_battery_level} %): the lowest charge limit the car allows.
• Max recommended charge limit ({max_recommended_charge_limit_battery_level} %): the car maker's recommendation.
• Preheat X min before ({preheat_minutes_before} min): preheat before leaving for work and trips (the preheat switch per weekday). In frost, the lead time is doubled.
entity_help.powerwall:
Home battery settings:
• Solar surplus only charges the car when the home battery is above the limit (now {ev_charge_after_powerwall_battery_level} %).
• Use the home battery for the car: needs Solar charging and Home battery discharge above needed turned on; only energy above the limit is used.
Create an automation that disables home battery discharging while the car charges, and only allows it when the switch is on and the battery is above the limit.
entity_help.virtual_ev:
Virtual EV (without a car integration):
• Virtual EV battery level: set the current battery level of the car when you plug it in.
• Completed charging level: the level the car stops at.
• Virtual EV max range: the realistic max range of the car.
entity_help.simulated_battery_level:
Simulated battery level (the car updates its battery level slowly):
• Car battery level: the value the car last reported.
• Simulated battery level: the car's last value plus what the charger's kWh meter has counted since, minus the charging loss. The plan and the charger actions use this one.
• When the car reports a new battery level, the simulation is corrected to the car's value (so it can jump a little) and keeps rising from there.
• You can enter the car's real battery level in Simulated battery level yourself, e.g. when you plug in and the car's value is behind. The simulation keeps rising from there until the car reports a new value. When you plug in, a notification asks if the value is right.
• The simulation stops 1 % below the car's charge limit, so the car itself confirms that charging is done.
• If it jumps a lot at every correction, the charging loss is off: measure it under Charging loss.
Turn it on or off in the integration's options under EV - sensors.
entity_help.forecast_auto: Choose the forecast type automatically: the house consumption and the car's distance per kWh each use the forecast type that was most accurate (the house consumption the last 30 days after 7 days of measurements, the distance per kWh the last 30 drives after 10 drives) and only switch when another type has at least 5 % less error. The selected forecast type is the starting point and is always used for the fallback prices and the solar history. See *Forecast accuracy* in the analysis.
entity_help.price_forecast: Correct the price forecast: the plan corrects the forecast prices (e.g. Carnot) by their average bias of the last 30 days, per day ahead – after 7 days of measurements, at most ±{price_correction_max} {valuta_kwh}. See *Price forecast* in the analysis.

dashboard.help_problem:
**A crash or error** (an error notification, *Error* as the charging rule, entities that stay unavailable) **or a wrong decision** (it charged when it shouldn't have, or didn't when it should, charged too much or too little - or the charging rule looks wrong):

1. Press **Export debug info** below **as soon as possible** - the file holds the latest calculations and log messages, older ones are replaced as time goes by.
2. A notification appears. Download the file and open the GitHub issue from the link in it (version and time are filled in).
3. Describe what happened and **when** (the time), which rule and charger action were shown, and what you expected instead. A screenshot of the plan helps.
4. Drag the file into the field *Debug file*.

The file is anonymised: no names, passwords, API keys, coordinates or addresses, entity names are replaced. Nothing is sent by itself - you decide what you upload.

dashboard.loss_intro: Measured continuously from the charger's kWh meter and the car's battery level, also back in Home Assistant's history. Only parts with the same power and phases all the way count.

dashboard.economy_intro: What the charging cost, compared with the same kWh charged in other ways while the car was plugged in at home. Solar and the home battery count with their value like in the plan.
dashboard.economy_subscription_intro: Compares each completed month's recorded charging-history cost with the fixed monthly price above. Solar and the home battery keep the same economic value as elsewhere in CJP. A positive difference means the subscription would have been cheaper. Only sessions recorded in CJP are included; public charging that was never recorded cannot be counted.
dashboard.economy_subscription_explain: Fixed monthly charging price: 0 disables the comparison. Only completed months are compared. The recorded cost includes solar and the home battery at their CJP economic value, so it is not necessarily the cash amount on the electricity bill. The comparison only covers sessions recorded in CJP; missing history can understate a month's cost. The price belongs to this car; do not enter the full price on several cars when one subscription covers them together.
dashboard.what_if_explain: A simulated comparison based on the history CJP has recorded. It never changes the live plan, the settings, the car or the charger, and it is an estimate, not a guaranteed or actual saving. The price field sets the subscription (0 disables it) and the table below compares it with each completed month. A chart shows the recorded cost against the fixed price per month.
dashboard.what_if_subscription_off: Enter a fixed monthly charging price above to compare it with the recorded charging cost.
dashboard.what_if_subscription_empty: No recorded charging months yet, so there is nothing to compare with the fixed monthly price.
dashboard.what_if_a_title: CJP against Smart and charging at once
dashboard.what_if_a_explain:
Compares what CJP actually charged with two other ways of charging at home over the same connections: **Smart** (the cheapest hours before the planned departure, up to the target level) and **Charging at once** (from plug-in to the same target). Smart and Charging at once use the grid only and have the same driving, charging loss, charging power and hourly prices. CJP is what was booked in the charging history, with solar and home battery at CJP's own value.

Settings: the **period** (from 7 days, at most the stored history), the **maximum recommended level** that the two charge to (0 uses the current setting), the **battery level at the first plug-in** (0 reads it from Home Assistant's history) and the **days** Smart is used on (on the other days Smart charges at once). Press **Run what-if** to calculate; nothing changes in the plan, the settings, the car or the charger.

Connections from before CJP started recording are estimated and marked ESTIMATE; a connection that cannot be read is skipped, and the card says why. The table shows energy charged, cost and price per kWh, and the differences (the other minus CJP, so positive means CJP was cheaper; for Smart against Charging at once, positive means Charging at once was cheaper). The adjusted difference accounts for the three ending at different battery levels. Differences marked ≈ are only an indication, because the three did not cover the same driving or the energy bought could not be balanced. The difference per year is scaled up from the period and is an ESTIMATE when there is less than a year of data or the period contains estimated connections. Below the table are a table per month, the coverage, warnings, assumptions and three charts.

This is a look back, not a guaranteed saving: Smart knows all prices in advance, charging elsewhere cannot be seen, and house limits and standby consumption are not included.

dashboard.what_if_warning_connections_modelled_fro: Connections before any record are modelled from the work plan as it is set now (homecoming, departure and distance per weekday), not recorded: the plan is not necessarily what happened. They are kept within the length of the longer measured connections.

dashboard.what_if_a_estimated_alert: ESTIMATE: part of the period is connections that were not measured but estimated from the battery level statistics or the work plan. When the car was connected is an estimate, so Smart, Charging at once and the differences are an estimate for that part. Measured connections replace it as CJP records them.
dashboard.what_if_a_estimated_booking: Before CJP's own records, what the car charged is estimated too: the charger energy from the hourly statistics, the solar share of it valued the way CJP values it, the rest at the grid price. The solar share is an upper bound (hourly means), which leans CJP's way, and the home battery counts as grid energy, which leans the other way
dashboard.what_if_a_booking_no_power_history: no hourly readings of the charger, solar and house power

dashboard.what_if_a_stop_not_settled: a session was still running or ended less than two hours ago
dashboard.what_if_a_estimates_none_available: No older connections could be estimated
dashboard.what_if_a_estimates_no_prices: The estimated connections have no stored prices, and no price is estimated for a connection that is itself an estimate.
dashboard.what_if_warning_recorded_segments: There are gaps in the data (connections that could not be read), so the connections are compared in several stretches. Each stretch has its own battery level at the start and at the end, read from the history; when the start level of a later stretch cannot be read, its first connection only brings the three to a common level. The totals are the sum of the stretches.
dashboard.what_if_a_stop_no_prices: no price was stored for it (no price is estimated for an estimated connection)
dashboard.what_if_warning_recorded_stretches_left_: Some stretches could not be compared (only one connection, which has no driving in it, or too few prices) and are left out.
dashboard.what_if_a_no_price_until: the newest one without a price ends
dashboard.what_if_a_estimates_no_record: The charging history of CJP does not reach the estimated connections before the measured ones.
dashboard.what_if_a_estimates_outside_charging: The estimated connections are not used: much of what CJP charged lies outside them, and that energy would be missing from the CJP column, which would make CJP look cheaper than it was.
dashboard.what_if_estimate_reason_no_statistics: the battery level statistics have no data
dashboard.what_if_estimate_reason_too_few_measured: too few measured connections to check the method against (at least 10)
dashboard.what_if_estimate_reason_not_validated: the method did not find the measured connections well enough
dashboard.what_if_estimate_reason_no_older_connect: the statistics show no connections before the measured ones
dashboard.what_if_estimate_reason_anchor_mismatch: the battery level at the first measured connection is not known from the statistics
dashboard.what_if_estimate_reason_no_workdays: the work plan has no workdays
dashboard.what_if_estimate_reason_too_few_drives: too few recorded drives to know the battery use per km (at least 10)
dashboard.what_if_estimate_reason_no_modelled_conn: the work plan gives no connections before the measured ones

dashboard.what_if_unit_only: The ≈ values are the CJP kWh at the price per kWh of Smart and of charging at once, against what CJP booked, and not a saving.

dashboard.what_if_reason_invalid_loss_model: The charging loss is not known
dashboard.what_if_reason_invalid_power_model: The learned charging power is invalid
dashboard.what_if_reason_energy_conservation: The energy balance did not add up, so the result is withheld
dashboard.what_if_reason_missing_prices: Fewer than half of the connections have a stored price, so there is nothing to estimate the rest from
dashboard.what_if_reason_interrupted: The calculation was interrupted by a restart

dashboard.what_if_reason_no_drives: No drive was recorded in the period, so the demand is unknown
dashboard.what_if_reason_no_days_selected: The day selection contains no days. Switch on workdays in the work plan or choose other days
dashboard.what_if_reason_start_level_stale: A connection ended while the starting level was read. Run it again
dashboard.what_if_reason_no_recorded_charging: No connection of the period can be read from the charging history of CJP (it does not reach back to them, or an entry is incomplete)
dashboard.what_if_reason_unmet_driving_differs: one of them cannot cover a different amount of driving
dashboard.what_if_warning_invalid_input_entries_le: Some recorded entries were invalid and left out. A missing drive understates the demand.
dashboard.what_if_warning_many_connections_without: Most connections have no recorded drive after them, so the demand is probably understated a lot.
dashboard.what_if_warning_connections_before_drive: Connections older than the oldest kept drive were left out because their demand is unknown.
dashboard.what_if_note_smart_hindsight_prices: Smart knows every price of the connection in advance (hindsight).
dashboard.what_if_note_energy_balanced_to_cjp: Over time the three must deliver the same energy: the energy CJP bought that no recorded drive explains (small trips, standby drain) is added as driving in all three.
dashboard.what_if_b_explain:
Replays your recorded history to compare your **current settings** with an **alternative daily reserve** and/or an **alternative maximum recommended level**. The reserve is the battery level the car should still have when it gets home; the maximum is the highest level CJP charges to. For each connection the replay charges in the cheapest hours up to the level the next trip needs plus the reserve, never above the maximum. Driving, connections, charging loss, charging power and hourly prices are the same for both settings.

Settings: the **period** and the **battery level at the first plug-in** (as in the comparison above), **What-if alternative daily return battery level** and **What-if EV max recommended charging limit** (0 uses the current setting, so a reserve of exactly 0 % cannot be tried; use 1). Press **Run what-if settings** to calculate; nothing changes in the plan, the settings, the car or the charger.

The table shows both settings with the reserve and maximum, energy charged, cost, the correction for the final battery level and the adjusted difference, which values a difference in the final battery level at the price per kWh actually paid, because a lower reserve ends lower (negative means the alternative was cheaper). If the two settings do not cover the same driving, the differences are only an indication, marked ≈, and the card says why. Below are a table per month, the coverage, the warnings and the assumptions, and two charts: cost per month for both settings and the accumulated difference.

This is a simplified model of CJP's planning rule, not CJP's planner, and it uses the current settings, because earlier settings are not stored. It is a look back in hindsight, not a guaranteed saving: the next trip is known in advance, and filling up in cheap hours, forced charging below the reserve, solar, house limits, standby consumption and a departure buffer are not included. The latest connection is left out because the trip after it is unknown. An hour without a price uses the price history or an estimated price. An unknown start level is set by the first connection, and the warnings say so. The reserve can have no effect when the maximum already decides the level.
dashboard.what_if_reason_no_change: Nothing to compare: both alternative values are 0 or equal to the current settings. Enter a different reserve or maximum level
dashboard.what_if_reason_invalid_settings: A reserve or maximum level is outside the allowed range
dashboard.what_if_reason_too_few_windows: At least two completed connections are needed, because the drive after the last one is unknown
dashboard.what_if_note_modelled_policy: A simplified model of the CJP planning rule, not of the CJP planner: charge in the cheapest hours to the next drive plus the reserve, capped at the maximum level.
dashboard.what_if_note_settings_history_not_stored: The current settings are replayed. Earlier settings are not stored, so this is not the plan CJP made at the time.
dashboard.what_if_note_last_connection_left_out: The latest connection is left out because the drive after it is not known yet.
dashboard.what_if_d_title: EV solar energy replaced by grid energy
dashboard.what_if_d_explain:
Shows what the energy your EV took from the sun would have cost if the car had charged at the same times from the grid and the sun had been sold. It is a simulated comparison based on the sessions CJP has recorded; it never changes anything, and it is an estimate, not a guaranteed saving.

For each finished private charging session with solar energy, the same kWh are priced twice: at the hourly grid buy price minus the refund, and at the sale the solar energy replaced, valued as CJP values it (the hourly sell price or the difference to your fixed production price). Solar energy is never treated as free. The solar advantage is the first minus the second; positive means the sun was cheaper than the grid. Both prices are time-weighted averages over the session.

The table shows per month sessions, charging hours, solar energy, the two values and the advantage. The total counts only completed months, and the month in progress is marked incomplete. Below it the card shows how many sessions were left out and why (for example public charging, still charging, no solar energy or a missing stored price), the home battery energy, which is kept as recorded, and the assumptions. No price is ever filled in. The table fills as new solar sessions are recorded.

If Home Assistant has long-term statistics for solar production, house consumption, charging power and sell price, charging hours that no recorded session covers are calculated hour by hour. This is an upper bound, because an hourly average cannot tell a short burst from slow charging: months and totals with such hours are marked with an asterisk, and the card shows the hours left out for a missing price. The comparison does not mean there was no solar production: it only shows what the car's solar energy would have cost from the grid. The home battery is not replaced, so no whole-house result is claimed. Two charts show the grid cost against the sale value and the accumulated solar advantage per month.
dashboard.what_if_d_reason_no_solar_configured: Solar is not set up in CJP, so there is no solar energy to replace
dashboard.what_if_d_reason_no_price_provider: No price provider is set up, so the refund on the buy price is unknown
dashboard.what_if_d_reason_waiting_for_new_session: Nothing to show yet: the comparison uses new charging sessions with solar energy and fills in as they are recorded
dashboard.what_if_d_reason_no_sell_prices: No sell prices have been stored for the sessions with solar yet. They are stored hour by hour, so the comparison fills in as the hours pass
dashboard.what_if_d_reason_no_buy_prices: No buy prices are stored for the sessions with solar
dashboard.what_if_d_reason_no_solar_sessions: No finished charging session with solar energy has been recorded
dashboard.what_if_d_left_not_captured: not priced in time (merged into the daily history first)
dashboard.what_if_d_note_solar_from_power_history: The solar energy is calculated hour by hour from the Home Assistant statistics of solar production, house consumption and charger power.
dashboard.what_if_d_note_production_price_assumed_: The production price of hours without a stored one is assumed to be the one set now.
dashboard.what_if_d_upper_bound: Includes charging hours that no recorded session covers, estimated from the hourly averages of the Home Assistant statistics. Their solar energy is an upper bound: an hourly average cannot tell a short burst of charging from slow charging all hour long. The money amounts of those hours scale with that energy, so they are not exact either.
dashboard.what_if_warning_energy_not_balanced: The battery level at the last unplug could not be read, so the three are not known to deliver the same energy: CJP may have bought energy that the recorded drives do not explain. No adjusted difference is given.
dashboard.what_if_note_booked_cost: The CJP cost is what CJP booked: one price per session (the price at the time CJP booked it, so it can differ from the hourly prices the session was charged at), with solar and the home battery at the value CJP gives them. Smart and Charging at once are grid only, so part of a difference can be solar.
dashboard.what_if_warning_windows_before_recorded_: Older connections are left out because the charging history of CJP does not reach them or cannot be read for one of them. Only the newest unbroken stretch is compared.
dashboard.what_if_warning_start_level_unknown_cali: The battery level at the first plug-in is unknown. The first connection is only used to bring the car to a common level (nothing is charged or counted in it) and the replay runs from the drives after it.
dashboard.what_if_warning_older_connections_not_va: The older connections suggested by the battery level statistics did not match the connections CJP measured itself well enough, so they are not used.
dashboard.what_if_warning_estimated_connections_wi: Estimated connections from before the first one with a stored price are left out: no price is estimated for a connection that is itself an estimate.
dashboard.what_if_price_estimate: Price used for hours without one (the average of the priced hours)
dashboard.what_if_ns_title: Without solar: planned from the grid
dashboard.what_if_ns_explain:
Takes the solar charging out and plans the period again using the grid only, with your current reserve, your maximum recommended level and your recorded driving: each connection is charged in the cheapest hours up to the level the next trip needs plus the reserve, never above the maximum, all at the hourly grid price.

Settings: the **period** (from 7 days, at most the stored history) and the **battery level at the first plug-in** (0 reads it from Home Assistant's history; if it is unknown, the first connection only brings the car to a common level). Press **Run what-if without solar** to calculate; nothing changes in the plan, the settings, the car or the charger.

The table shows the planned grid-only charging next to CJP over the same period, with the solar valued as CJP values it: energy charged, cost, price per kWh and solar energy, with the reserve and maximum used. The difference is the plan without solar minus CJP. The estimate line values the energy CJP charged at the plan's price per kWh and shows the **difference vs plan**; positive means CJP's charging cost more. It is not the value of the solar energy: it also contains differences in charging times and price choices, and CJP's energy contains short trips and standby consumption that the replay does not have. Read it as a rough size, not a saving. It needs recorded solar energy, which connections from before CJP stored it do not have.

Below are a table per month, the coverage, the estimated price, any home battery energy in CJP's charging (kept as it is), the warnings and the assumptions, and three charts: cost, price per kWh and energy per month.

Connections from before CJP started recording are estimated from the battery level and charging power statistics or modelled from the work plan and come first in the calculation. What CJP charged in them is estimated in the same way as in the comparison above (with the solar taken off) and only appears in the table per month; a month only gets a CJP figure and a difference when all its connections have one. Hours without a stored price use the price history, otherwise an estimated price (the average of the hours that have a price); if fewer than half of the connections have prices, there is no result. The latest connection is left out because the trip after it is unknown. Not included: house limits, standby consumption, a departure buffer, charging in cheap hours and forced charging below the reserve.

dashboard.what_if_ns_difference_vs_plan_note: Positive means CJP's charging cost more than the same energy at the plan's price per kWh. This is not the value of the solar energy: it also includes when the charging happened and at which prices.
dashboard.what_if_ns_no_recorded: No private charging by CJP in the period to compare with.

dashboard.what_if_d_powerwall: Home battery energy in these sessions, kept as it is and not replaced
dashboard.economy_explain: *Paid: the cost of the charging, with the price per kWh next to it. Avg.: the average price while the car was plugged in. Daily: like most smart chargers – cheapest until the next departure (work plan), without waiting for a cheaper night. Lowest: the cheapest hours of the whole time plugged in (knows every price beforehand, so 100 % is close to impossible). Score: how close the price came to the lowest, measured from the average (100 % = the cheapest hours, 0 % = the average price). {valuta}/{distance}: all charging incl. public divided by the {distance} driven. Saved: what daily charging would have cost for the same kWh, minus what was paid – a comparison, not a guaranteed saving. The two charts show the kWh per source and the prices against the references. The comparison only exists for periods with known plug-in times (from the installation and, before that, as far back as the Home Assistant history reached).*
dashboard.drive_temperature_fit_1: For every degree colder the car drives
dashboard.drive_temperature_fit_2: less ({distance} per kWh from the battery):
dashboard.drive_temperature_no_data: Too few drives with a temperature yet – at least 5 drives at different temperatures are needed
dashboard.departures_met_1: The car had the required battery level at
dashboard.departures_no_data: No departures saved yet – they are saved from now on at every work plan departure
dashboard.learn_distance_on: *Learn driving distance* is on: the plan uses the higher of the entered and the learned value once there are enough days. The entered values are not changed.
dashboard.learn_distance_off: *Learn driving distance* is off: the learned values are only a suggestion, the plan uses the entered ones.
dashboard.learn_distance_no_data: No days measured yet – the odometer is read every evening at 23:59, the first day's distance comes after two evenings
dashboard.learn_distance_explain: *Every evening at 23:59 the odometer is read, and the day's driving is the difference from the evening before. Evenings CJP did not read itself are fetched from Home Assistant's history. Entered: what is set in the work plan and under optimal weekly charging, which the plan uses. Learned: a typical distance for the weekday based on the last 8 weeks; for the typical daily distance, based on all days. Days: number of measured days; ⏳ means there are still too few for the figure to be used. With *Learn driving distance* turned on, the plan uses the higher of the entered and the learned distance once there are enough days. The entered values are not changed.*
dashboard.planned_summary_3: of it outside the plan (manual, forced charging etc.):
dashboard.planned_no_data: No days saved yet – the plan for the next day is saved from now on every evening at 23:59
dashboard.capacity_title: kWh from the charger per 1 % per month
dashboard.capacity_explain: *If the number rises over the years, the battery holds less (or the charging loss rose). In winter it is higher, because the car uses energy to heat the battery. So compare the same month year by year and the same power group.*
dashboard.drive_temperature_explain: *Every drive from unplugging to plugging in again, with the outdoor temperature (the mean while the car was away) and {distance_kwh} from the odometer and the battery level (with the battery size set in CJP). The orange line is the average per 5 °C. The trend shows how much {distance_kwh} changes per degree and what the cold costs. Drives under 5 {distance} or under 2 % battery are left out. The first time the drives of the last days are read from the Home Assistant history, from then on every drive is recorded.*
dashboard.departures_explain: *At every departure of the work plan the battery level the car left with is compared with the requirement: the day's driving plus the daily minimum level (✅ = met). The plan's target is the level the plan aimed for before work. Only departures from now on are saved (the plans of the past are not kept), the last 14 are shown.*
dashboard.planned_explain: *Every evening at 23:59 the kWh the plan expects to charge the next day are saved. Here they are compared with what was actually charged that day. Outside the plan = manual charging, charging because the battery was low and other charging. Public charging is not counted.*
dashboard.price_forecast_intro: The price integration's forecast against the real price, the last 30 days:
dashboard.price_forecast_unit: Error and bias in {valuta_kwh}. In brackets: the extra price per kWh of picking the hours by the forecast.
dashboard.price_forecast_no_data: Collected from now on: the first numbers at 13:00 tomorrow, when the real prices of the day after come.
dashboard.price_forecast_correction_off: The correction of the price forecast is off (*Settings → Advanced*).
dashboard.price_forecast_correction_waiting: The forecast is corrected per day ahead after 7 days of measurements.
dashboard.price_forecast_explain: Every hour CJP saves the buy price from the price integration's forecast (without CJP's own adder per day ahead) for the coming days. When the real prices of a day arrive (around 13:00 the day before), they are compared with what the forecast said 1, 2, 3 … days before. **Error** is the average error per hour, whether the forecast was too high or too low. **Bias** > 0: the forecast was too high. **Worst hour**: the largest error in a single hour. **Cheapest found**: how many of the day's 4 cheapest hours by the forecast really were among the 4 cheapest – the hours the plan prefers to charge the car in. The extra price in brackets is what picking by the forecast instead of the real hours cost per kWh. The chart shows the real prices and the forecasts of the last and the coming days. A second chart shows the error per day. **Correction**: with *Correct the price forecast* on, the plan adjusts the forecast prices for each day ahead by their average **Bias** of the last 30 days (a forecast that was too high is lowered), after at least 7 days of measurements and by at most ±{price_correction_max} {valuta_kwh}. The chart then also shows *Forecast used (corrected)*.
dashboard.soc_power_explain: The chart and table show how much power the car can charge with at different battery levels, and whether it is 1 or 3 phases. When a level has repeatedly shown clearly slower charging than a lower level, CJP learns a limit and the plan uses it, so it does not count on more power than the car actually takes. The table also shows how many charges have stable measurements and how many showed slower charging; at least 3 are needed for a limit. Until a level has its own measurements, stable hourly figures from Home Assistant's statistics are used as a starting value (marked 📊). This is only a planning calculation and does not control the charger. The switch turns the use of the learned limits in the plan on or off; the measurements are collected either way.
dashboard.soc_power_chart_title: Learned charging power by battery level
dashboard.forecast_consumption_intro: House consumption per hour in kWh
dashboard.forecast_better: ⭐ {best} forecast the house consumption best the last 30 days: on average {best_mae} kWh off per hour against {selected_mae} kWh for the selected ✅ {selected} ({percent} % less error). The actual consumption was {actual} kWh per hour; {best} expected {best_forecast} kWh and {selected} {selected_forecast} kWh. With *Choose the forecast type automatically* on, the most accurate type is used by itself.
dashboard.forecast_better_drives: ⭐ {best} forecast the car's {distance_kwh} best on the last drives: on average {best_mae} {distance_kwh} off per drive against {selected_mae} {distance_kwh} for the selected ✅ {selected} ({percent} % less error). The car actually drove {actual} {distance_kwh}; {best} expected {best_forecast} {distance_kwh} and {selected} {selected_forecast} {distance_kwh}. With *Choose the forecast type automatically* on, the most accurate type is used by itself.
dashboard.forecast_auto_on: 🔄 The forecast type is chosen automatically: the house consumption now uses ✅ {selected}, the most accurate the last 30 days. It only switches when another type has at least 5 % less error.
dashboard.forecast_auto_on_drives: 🔄 The forecast type is chosen automatically: the {distance_kwh} now uses ✅ {selected}, the most accurate on the last drives. It only switches when another type has at least 5 % less error.
dashboard.forecast_auto_waiting: 🔄 The automatic choice for the house consumption starts after {days} days of measurements. Until then the selected ✅ {manual} is used.
dashboard.forecast_auto_waiting_drives: 🔄 The automatic choice for the {distance_kwh} starts after {drives} drives. Until then the selected ✅ {manual} is used.
dashboard.forecast_no_data: Collected from now on: the house consumption after the first whole day, {distance_kwh} after the first drive.
dashboard.forecast_explain:
Just before a new measurement is added to the history (the house consumption every hour, the car's {distance_kwh} after every drive), CJP calculates what each forecast type would have predicted from the same history and compares it with the measurement. ✅ the forecast type in use, ⭐ the most accurate. **Avg.** is what each type expected on average, against the actual value at the top. The **error** is counted hour by hour / drive by drive, so a type can hit the average and still miss a lot each time. **Bias** > 0: the forecast was too high.

The forecast type (*Settings → Advanced → Forecast type*) applies to the house consumption, {distance_kwh} and the fallback prices alike, so pick the one that is most accurate where it matters most. With *Choose the forecast type automatically* on, the house consumption and {distance_kwh} each use their most accurate type instead (after 7 days of measurements / 10 drives) and only switch when another type has at least 5 % less error; the fallback prices and the solar history keep the selected type. The house consumption is only used for the solar surplus; {distance_kwh} for how much trips and workdays need.
dashboard.history_explain:
* **Battery level and charging limit**: the last 48 hours (and the simulated battery level when it is on).
* **Driving efficiency**: the last 30 days.
* **Charged by solar**: the last 7 days.
